title: Internal cycloidal actuator
summary: A 15:1 cycloidal gearbox packaged inside a custom BLDC stator, with a 55 mm axial length.
description: A compact robotic actuator combining a custom BLDC motor with an internal dual-disc cycloidal gearbox. The completed project packages a 15:1 mechanical reduction in a 55 mm axial envelope.
objectives: Package a 15:1 reduction inside the stator to minimize axial length.
Develop low-cost closed-loop position control using a microcontroller and encoder.
contributions: Researched cycloidal kinematics and generated parametric disc profiles in SolidWorks.
Designed the 100-part assembly around available bearings, fasteners, and existing motor components.

process.title: Balance the eccentric motion
process.body: Two cycloidal discs offset by 180° balance the rotating mass. The cycloidal architecture was chosen to target low backlash; measured backlash has not been supplied.

process.title: Work within the stator
process.body: M6 steel dowels replace conventional ring-gear bearings to reduce the radial footprint. Parametric profiles accommodate the available bearing sizes.

process.title: Resolve the packaging constraint
process.body: The documented design is 55 mm long. Off-the-shelf component interference prevented the original sub-50 mm target; shorter, custom-machined pins were identified as a future improvement.

results: Documented mechanical design: 15:1 reduction, 55 mm axial length, and 100 parts.
lessons: Commercial component dimensions can set the limit on an otherwise compact design.
